title: Coefficient at an indecomposable ideal exponent gives a residue quotient
statement:
Let $P$ be a commutative additive monoid with identity $0$ which is cancellative ($x+z=y+z$ implies $x=y$) and sharp ($x+y=0$ implies $x=y=0$). Let $J\subseteq K\subseteq P$ satisfy $J+P\subseteq J$ and $K+P\subseteq K$, allowing $J=\varnothing$. Suppose $p\in K\setminus J$ and $p\notin K+(P\setminus\{0\})$. Put $R=\mathbf Z[P]=\bigoplus_{q\in P}\mathbf Z e_q$, with $e_qe_r=e_{q+r}$ and $e_0=1$. For a monoid ideal $I$ let $IR=(e_i:i\in I)\subseteq R$, and put $\mathfrak m=(e_q:q\ne0)\subseteq R$. Then $IR=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbf Z e_i$, and $KR/JR$ has the $\mathbf Z$-basis $\{[e_k]:k\in K\setminus J\}$. The map $\varepsilon:R\to\mathbf Z$, $\sum_qn_qe_q\mapsto n_0$, is a ring homomorphism with kernel $\mathfrak m$, so $R/\mathfrak m\cong\mathbf Z$. With $R$ acting on $\mathbf Z$ through $\varepsilon$, coefficient at $p$ defines a surjective $R$-linear map
$$\varphi_p:KR/JR\twoheadrightarrow\mathbf Z,\qquad [\sum_kn_ke_k]\longmapsto n_p.$$
For every commutative ring $A$ and ring homomorphism $f:R\to A$, put $\mathfrak mA=(f(e_q):q\ne0)$. Tensoring $\varphi_p$ with $A$, using the ordinary module tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], gives a surjective $A$-linear map
$$\Phi_p:(KR/JR)\otimes_RA\twoheadrightarrow A/\mathfrak mA,\qquad [r]\otimes b\longmapsto r_p b\bmod\mathfrak mA,$$
where $r_p\in\mathbf Z$ is the coefficient of $e_p$ in $r\in KR$.

proof.text: For any monoid ideal $I$, let $S_I$ be the subgroup of finite sums supported in $I$. Multiplication by $e_q$ preserves $S_I$, since $i+q\in I$ for $i\in I$; expanding an arbitrary multiplier as a finite sum shows that $S_I$ is a ring ideal. It contains every $e_i$, so $IR\subseteq S_I$. Conversely each $n_i e_i$ belongs to $IR$, hence $S_I\subseteq IR$. This proves the asserted direct-sum description, including $I=\varnothing$.

proof.text: Deleting the coordinates indexed by $J$ defines an additive map $KR\to\bigoplus_{k\in K\setminus J}\mathbf Z$. Its kernel is precisely the sums supported in $J$, namely $JR$ by step 1. Its inverse on the quotient sends a finitely supported family $(n_k)$ to $[\sum n_ke_k]$: reinserting and deleting coordinates are inverse because their difference is supported in $J$. Thus the classes $[e_k]$ form the stated $\mathbf Z$-basis.

proof.text: Sharpness says that $q+r=0$ only when $q=r=0$. Expanding two finite sums therefore gives $(ab)_0=a_0b_0$, while addition and the unit are respected coordinatewise. Hence $\varepsilon$ is a ring homomorphism. Its kernel is exactly the sums supported away from $0$; these form $\mathfrak m$ by step 1, since sharpness also makes $P\setminus\{0\}$ a monoid ideal. The inverse of the induced map $R/\mathfrak m\to\mathbf Z$ is $n\mapsto[ne_0]$, as $r-r_0e_0\in\mathfrak m$.

For $a\in R$ and $r\in KR$, expand their product. A term contributing at $p$ has indices $q\in P$, $k\in K$ with $q+k=p$. If $q
e0$, this contradicts $p
otin K+(P\setminus\{0\})$. Thus only $(q,k)=(0,p)$ contributes, and $(ar)_p=a_0r_p$. Coefficient at $p$ vanishes on $JR$, because $p
otin J$, so it descends to $\varphi_p$; this identity proves $R$-linearity for the stated action. Since $\varphi_p([ne_p])=n$ for every integer $n$, it is surjective.

proof.text: Put $B=A/\mathfrak mA$ and write $\bar b$ for the class of $b$. Finite expansion gives $\overline{f(a)}=a_0\bar1$ for $a\in R$. The map $\beta(n,b)=n\bar b$ is additive in each variable and $R$-bilinear: $\beta(a\cdot n,b)=a_0n\bar b=\overline{f(a)}n\bar b=\beta(n,f(a)b)$, with the same value equal to $a\cdot\beta(n,b)$. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives $\theta:\mathbf Z\otimes_RA\to B$, $n\otimes b\mapsto n\bar b$. The additive map $b\mapsto1\otimes b$ is $A$-linear for the action $c(n\otimes b)=n\otimes cb$. Every element of $\mathfrak mA$ is a finite sum $\sum_i f(e_{q_i})b_i$ with $q_i\ne0$. Its image is $\sum_i1\otimes f(e_{q_i})b_i=\sum_i(e_{q_i}\cdot1)\otimes b_i=0$, since $\varepsilon(e_{q_i})=0$. It induces $\eta:B\to\mathbf Z\otimes_RA$. The map $\theta$ is also $A$-linear, as $\theta(n\otimes cb)=c\theta(n\otimes b)$. Finally $\theta\eta(\bar b)=\bar b$ and $\eta\theta(n\otimes b)=1\otimes nb=n\otimes b$, so the maps are inverse by generation by pure tensors. The action used here respects the defining bilinearity relations, because multiplying the second factor by $c$ commutes with $f(a)$ in the commutative ring $A$.

proof.text: By the tensor-map formula in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], compose $\varphi_p\otimes\mathrm{id}_A$ with $\theta$ of step 5. On pure tensors the composite is $[r]\otimes b\mapsto r_p\bar b$, exactly $\Phi_p$. On the source tensor product the action $c([r]\otimes b)=[r]\otimes cb$ respects the bilinearity relations because $cf(a)=f(a)c$. Multiplication by $c\in A$ replaces $b$ with $cb$, proving $A$-linearity on generators and hence everywhere. Every $\bar b\in B$ is the image of $[e_p]\otimes b$, so $\Phi_p$ is surjective. This also works if $B=0$, without a flatness hypothesis on $A$.

lean.statement: theorem monomial_quotient_residue_surjection (P : Type u) [AddCancelCommMonoid P] (hsharp : ∀ x y : P, x + y = 0 → x = 0 ∧ y = 0) (J K : Set P) (hJK : J ⊆ K) (hJ : ∀ j ∈ J, ∀ q : P, j + q ∈ J) (hK : ∀ k ∈ K, ∀ q : P, k + q ∈ K) (p : P) (hpK : p ∈ K) (hpJ : p ∉ J) (hp : ∀ k ∈ K, ∀ q : P, q ≠ 0 → k + q ≠ p) : (∀ (I : Set P), (∀ i ∈ I, ∀ q : P, i + q ∈ I) → ∀ r : AddMonoidAlgebra ℤ P, r ∈ monomialSpan I ↔ ∀ q : P, r.coeff q ≠ 0 → q ∈ I) ∧ (∃ b : Module.Basis {k : P // k ∈ K \ J} ℤ (monomialQuotient J K), ∀ k : {k : P // k ∈ K \ J}, b k = Submodule.Quotient.mk ⟨of' ℤ P k.val, Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_image_of_mem _ k.property.1)⟩) ∧ ∃ ε : AddMonoidAlgebra ℤ P →+* ℤ, (∀ r : AddMonoidAlgebra ℤ P, ε r = r.coeff 0) ∧ RingHom.ker ε = monomialSpan {q : P | q ≠ 0} ∧ (∃ e : (AddMonoidAlgebra ℤ P ⧸ monomialSpan {q : P | q ≠ 0}) ≃+* ℤ, ∀ r : AddMonoidAlgebra ℤ P, e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (monomialSpan {q : P | q ≠ 0}) r) = ε r) ∧ (∃ φ : monomialQuotient J K →ₛₗ[ε] ℤ, Function.Surjective φ ∧ ∀ r : monomialSpan K, φ (Submodule.Quotient.mk r) = r.val.coeff p) ∧ ∀ (A : Type v) [CommRing A] [Algebra (AddMonoidAlgebra ℤ P) A], ∃ Φ : (monomialQuotient J K ⊗[AddMonoidAlgebra ℤ P] A) →+ (A ⧸ monomialResidueIdeal P A), Function.Surjective Φ ∧ (∀ (c : A) (x : monomialQuotient J K ⊗[AddMonoidAlgebra ℤ P] A), Φ ((LinearMap.lTensor (monomialQuotient J K) (LinearMap.mulLeft (AddMonoidAlgebra ℤ P) c)) x) = c • Φ x) ∧ ∀ (r : monomialSpan K) (b : A), Φ ((Submodule.Quotient.mk r) ⊗ₜ[AddMonoidAlgebra ℤ P] b) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (monomialResidueIdeal P A) ((r.val.coeff p : A) * b)
